_meta.judge: self-rated by the writer; see prompts/clue_judge.md

critique.weakest_clue: OFFSPRING ("Next generation, collectively") is a plain definition; I dropped the better "Issue for parents?" because the decoy PARENTING half-fits it.
critique.weakest_word: INSURER: a dull word rescued only by its pun clue.
critique.notes: Two "?" puns in a row risk feeling samey. The SPR tile appears twice (SPRINTER, OFFSPRING), a nice shared anchor.

critique.weakest_clue: ATTACKING: straight definition of a bland participle.
critique.weakest_word: ATTACKING (inflected, nothing to play with); COVER is short and only 2 tiles.
critique.notes: "Comet or Cupid" sits next to ASTEROID on purpose: the solver's first thought is astronomy. SCEPTER uses the American spelling.

UNANSWERED.clue: Like a call that rings out

critique.weakest_clue: RESISTANT: the fill-in is serviceable, not clever, and "waterproof" does a lot of the work.
critique.weakest_word: UNANSWERED: 10 letters split 2-3-3-2, long and a little clinical.
critique.notes: "Missing class" should read as "lacking style" first. Decoys RESISTING / RESISTED / RANGER / TWISTER make this pool busy.

CHUCKLE.clue: Polite response to a dad joke

critique.weakest_clue: UNDERWENT ("Endured, as surgery") is the flattest clue in the batch.
critique.weakest_word: UNDERWENT: an irregular past tense is no fun to clue or to find.
critique.notes: The theme label is a deliberate nudge toward RAINING; I dropped the fill-in "___ cats and dogs" because the sub-word RAIN (RA+IN) completes it too. Tiles IND and END/ENT/AND are nicely confusable.

PATIENT.clue: Calm sort in a waiting room?

critique.weakest_clue: SEMESTER ("Half a school year") is a dictionary definition.
critique.weakest_word: WONDERING: inflected filler; CONVERT is fine but colourless.
critique.notes: Three "?" clues is one too many for a single round. PATIENT's clue leans on both senses of the word, which some solvers find too easy.

critique.weakest_clue: PRESENTED ("Handed over, as a trophy"): flat, and the word gives nothing to work with.
critique.weakest_word: PRESENTED (inflected, dull). UNDERCOVER's tiles UN-DE-RCO-VER include the ugly 3-consonant-ish RCO.
critique.notes: Theme label quotes the TORTOISE clue. Many 2-letter tiles here (8 of 21), so it plays a bit easier than the score suggests.

INFLATION.clue: It makes balloons and prices rise

critique.weakest_clue: INSTALLING ("Putting in, as software").
critique.weakest_word: INSTALLING: inflected and technical. STAIRCASE and SUITCASE both end in tile ASE, which is the point, but they also rhyme visually, which makes the pair fall together.
critique.notes: Best structural round for shared tiles (ASE twice, STA/STR/ST, ING twice). Theme label hints at STAIRCASE.

critique.weakest_clue: COMPONENT ("Stereo part") is vague; could be many things.
critique.weakest_word: RESIDING and COMPONENT are both dry.
critique.notes: Weakest clue set I wrote (five definitions); by taste I would drop it before any of the rounds cut on score, so I did.
critique.verdict_reason: Editor override: five flat definitions; the formula kept it on tile structure alone.

PREACHING.clue: Wasting a sermon on the choir

critique.weakest_clue: PROCEED ("Green light's message") is fine but ordinary.
critique.weakest_word: SEPARATELY: an adverb, 10 letters in 4 tiles (SE-PAR-ATE-LY); the clue carries it.
critique.notes: My favourite clue set. OYSTER's clue needs the idiom "the world is your oyster"; solvers who miss it still get it from OYS. PREACHING lost its fill-in clue ("___ to the choir") because the sub-word PREACH (PRE+ACH) completes the blank too.

HONEYMOON.clue: Trip for two after the I do's

critique.weakest_clue: INVITE ("Ask to the party").
critique.weakest_word: SCALING: inflected, and the clue's fish sense may feel like a stretch to some.
critique.notes: HON appears twice (HONEYMOON, MARATHON) and INT/INV are near-twins. HONEYMOON's tile EYM is an ugly anchor.

GLITTER.clue: Craft sparkle you never fully vacuum

critique.weakest_clue: LAVENDER ("Sachet scent"): accurate, but "sachet" is not an everyday word.
critique.weakest_word: INTERNAL: plain adjective. MOOSE is only 5 letters (MOO+SE).
critique.notes: DER appears twice (LAVENDER, CONTENDER) and VEN/DEN/TEN/VER/TER are all one letter apart, so this pool is properly slippery.

INTERVIEW.clue: Hot seat for a job seeker

critique.weakest_clue: INHERENT ("Built-in"): correct, colourless.
critique.weakest_word: INHERENT and IMPENDING: two abstract IN-/IM- adjectives in one round.
critique.notes: Four answers start with IN-/IM- tiles (IMP, INT, INH, INL): good ambiguity, but the first tiles are one letter apart rather than shared, so it is more fiddly than tricky.

PROPOSAL.clue: It may end with a ring

critique.weakest_clue: CLUSTER ("Tight bunch").
critique.weakest_word: INSTRUCTOR: long and businesslike; PROVOKING is inflected.
critique.notes: PRO twice and POR/POS/PO near-twins. Theme label repeats a word from the GOSSIP clue.

critique.weakest_clue: CONFUSED ("All mixed up"): flat, though it winks at the tile jumble.
critique.weakest_word: INVERSE: schoolroom word. CENTAUR's clue is a definition and STALLION makes "horse" a visible cross-hint.
critique.notes: ION twice (STALLION, ACCORDION). Decoy CONFUSION (CON+FUS+ION) is a real trap for the CONFUSED clue; the clue's adjective form is what rules it out.

critique.weakest_clue: COMBINING ("Mixing together").
critique.weakest_word: COMBINING: inflected filler. INSOMNIA's tile SOM/NIA are both anchors, so it falls quickly.
critique.notes: I changed COMPLAINT's clue from bare "Beef" because the decoy COMPLAIN (COM+PLA+IN) would have fit it as a verb. COM twice.

critique.weakest_clue: SPATULA ("Pancake flipper") is the obvious clue.
critique.weakest_word: RELENTLESS: tiles RE-LE-NTL-ESS; NTL is a vowel-less giveaway. STAINLESS shares ESS with it (intended) but also the -LESS ending, which is a bit repetitive.
critique.notes: Thunder in one clue and LIGHTNING as another answer is a small cross-hint. Theme label quotes the LIGHTNING clue.

critique.weakest_clue: CONFUSION ("Fog of bewilderment") is wordy for what it does.
critique.weakest_word: RIDER: 5 letters, 2 tiles; CONFUSION is abstract.
critique.notes: CON twice, TRO/TRA twins, and the decoy CONTRACT (CON+TRA+CT) is sitting in the pool while RIDER's clue says "Contract".

TRANSFORM.clue: Go from Clark Kent to Superman

critique.weakest_clue: RENDERING ("Architect's 3D preview"): narrow sense of the word.
critique.weakest_word: RENDERING: inflected-looking and technical.
critique.notes: AST twice (ASTRONAUT, COASTER); TRI/TRA and REF/REN twins. TRANSFORM's tiles TRA-NSF-ORM contain the ugly NSF.

MECHANIC.clue: One who works under the hood

critique.weakest_clue: MECHANIC ("One who works under the hood").
critique.weakest_word: PREDICTED: inflected, but it earns its place through the clue.
critique.notes: NIC twice (MECHANIC, TITANIC), TRI/CRI twins, and lots of short real-word decoys (TICKET, TICKLE, TACKLE, TRICKLE). Seven 2-letter tiles.

INTENSE.clue: Extreme, as heat or a stare

critique.weakest_clue: REASONING ("Thinking it through"): reworded so the decoy REASON does not also fit, at the cost of some life.
critique.weakest_word: REASONING: abstract; INTENSE is plain.
critique.notes: PUNCHLINE's CHL tile is a dead giveaway. "Funny" and "Joke" in neighbouring clues overlap in flavour. Theme label quotes the PECULIAR clue.

critique.weakest_clue: THANKFUL ("In a November mood?") assumes US Thanksgiving.
critique.weakest_word: DECLINING: inflected; MASTERMIND's tiles MAS-TE-RM-IND are choppy.
critique.notes: FUL twice (THANKFUL, WONDERFUL) and TER twice (WAITER, SPLINTER); decoys MASTERFUL, WONDERING, BLINDING. Theme label quotes the BLENDER clue.

WANDERING.clue: Like an idle mind or a minstrel

critique.weakest_clue: BATTALION ("Army unit of several companies") is an encyclopedia entry.
critique.weakest_word: BATTALION: the least friendly word here.
critique.notes: MAG twice and IC twice, so MAGIC / MAGICAL / MAGNETIC are all spellable decoys. WILDERNESS splits WIL-DE-RN-ESS; RN is harsh.

critique.weakest_clue: REPORTEDLY ("According to sources").
critique.weakest_word: REPORTEDLY: an adverb; BELFRY may be unfamiliar to younger solvers.
critique.notes: Structurally the least tangled round I clued: few shared tiles, several anchors (NDM, LCA, FRY). It was a candidate for the words and clues alone.

critique.weakest_clue: APPALLING ("Shockingly bad").
critique.weakest_word: RENEW: 5 letters, 2 tiles, plain. COCKTAIL's CKT tile is an instant anchor.
critique.notes: ALL twice and MAR twice. "Shaken or stirred" will make people look for MARTINI, and MAR+TI is right there (MARTIAL). Theme label quotes that clue.
